question: Has anyone anywhere ever delivered radiotherapy to lung metastases in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma, and is there a concept paper in it?

provenance.note: Every identifier below was returned by a Europe PMC query recorded in the citation index. Where a statement comes from an abstract rather than full text, the record says so, because an abstract is evidence of what a paper claims and not of how it got there.

headline: ANSWER: YES — at least seven reported deliveries, and the rationale for doing it is ALREADY IN PRINT. ⛔ CORRECTED 2026-08-10, same day: this file first said the field had never drawn the distinction between conventionally fractionated dose to a primary and ablative dose to a metastasis. IT HAS. The 2025 comprehensive review (PMID 41055792) states in its own words that 'Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) may also be an option instead of surgery', that 'Metastasis-directed local therapy should follow uniform MDT criteria', that hypofractionation at 3-5 Gy per fraction 'may have contributed to overcoming the intrinsic radioresistance of EMC', and that conventional EBRT regimens 'typically deliver BED levels insufficient for long-term control' against a BED of 142 Gy at alpha/beta = 4. That is the argument this artifact claimed was unstated, stated more precisely than it was claimed. What remains true and unchanged: nobody has assembled the reported cases into a dose-and-outcome table, and no series, trial or registry analysis has evaluated the practice.

direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.title: Excellent Response and Persistent Local Control of Metastatic Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma Repeatedly Treated with Surgical Excision or Stereotactic Radiotherapy Alone: A Case Report
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.read_from: UPDATED 2026-08-28 (AUT-RT-001): FULL TEXT, fetched at $0 via a plain HTTPS GET to pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12659415/ from a GitHub Actions runner (fetch-literature.yml, slug=emc-rt-pmid-41323055, run 33178734185) -- HTTP 200, 24,678 chars, committed to the literature-cache branch at literature/emc-rt-pmid-41323055/pmc_plain_new_domain.txt. ⚠ Superseded, retained: the publisher (Karger) page itself still 403s a plain fetch from both the sandbox and a runner, exactly as previously recorded; PMC's own copy of this open-access article did not, and had not been tried before this pass.
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.what_it_reports: One patient (39-year-old woman, right-thigh EMC, 2019). Metastatic disease was managed with THREE SABR occasions (Sept 2023; Dec 2024, delivered as two sub-courses at different doses for different lesion locations; March 2025) interposed with ONE surgical excision (June 2024, of a single new nodule) -- reconciling the abstract's 'surgical excision or SABR alone in three different occasions' with Table 1's four numbered 'SABR courses' (the Dec-2024 occasion split into two dose plans). Full dose/fractionation/outcome detail is now in `dose_outcome_table` below. Every irradiated site remained free of local relapse through the paper's last reported restaging (March 2025); new lesions kept appearing at OTHER sites (oligoprogression), which is why repeated SABR was needed, but no previously-treated site ever relapsed.
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.weight: n = 1, no control, and the authors present it as an individualised approach for selected patients rather than as a general claim.
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.why_it_matters: It is the only paper in the searchable record in which ablative radiotherapy is the deliberate, repeated, sole treatment of metastatic EMC, and it is now the only entry in this artifact with a complete, source-read dose/fractionation record for MULTIPLE separate ablative deliveries in the same patient.

direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.title: Whole Lung Radiotherapy to Treat Metastatic Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcomas
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.read_from: title, journal, year, PMID and DOI from the Europe PMC record; NO abstract is indexed and the publisher page returns HTTP 403, so the content statement below rests on a search-engine snippet and has NOT been verified against the paper
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.what_it_reports: UNVERIFIED, flagged: two patients with metastatic EMC reported as having sustained symptomatic benefit from bilateral whole-lung external beam radiotherapy.
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.weight: n = 2, symptomatic endpoint, and the primary text has not been read here.
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.outstanding: Obtain the full text before any figure or outcome from this paper is quoted anywhere.

direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.title: High-dose-rate interstitial brachytherapy as a suitable option for metastatic extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma - a case report
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.modality: HDR interstitial brachytherapy, 30 Gy in 2 fractions in one day
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.what_it_reports: One patient, 87 years old. Three separate metastatic sites treated (inguinal node, breast, popliteal fossa); long-term local control at all three without severe acute or late toxicity.
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.weight: n = 1. Not lung, but it is a direct observation of metastatic EMC responding durably to ablative dose.
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.why_it_matters: Three sites in one patient controlled by radiation alone is a harder observation to attribute to indolence than a single treated lesion is.

direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.title: The role of radiotherapy and chemotherapy in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.what_it_reports: In the 29-patient metastatic-at-presentation subgroup, two patients received palliative radiotherapy for metastatic lesions. No outcome is reported for those two.
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.weight: The exposure is recorded; the outcome is not. This is the only cohort in which metastasis-directed radiotherapy appears at all, and it appears as an untabulated line.
direct_evidence_rt_to_emc_metastases.why_it_matters: It establishes that the practice happens in real cohorts and that nobody has ever reported what it did.

adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.title: Extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma in the pelvis successfully treated with proton beam radiotherapy
adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.what_it_reports: A man in his late 60s with pelvic EMC maintained a COMPLETE RESPONSE for more than seven years on proton beam radiotherapy with intra-arterial chemotherapy, without surgery.
adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.why_it_matters: A seven-year complete response is difficult to reconcile with a tumour described as refractory to radiotherapy, and it is a primary rather than a metastasis.

adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.title: Locally recurrent extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma of the shoulder: a case of complete neoadjuvant radiotherapy response
adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.what_it_reports: Preoperative radiotherapy, 50 Gy; the resection specimen contained NO VIABLE TUMOUR CELLS; no relapse at 24 months.
adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.why_it_matters: A pathological complete response is the strongest single observation against the radioresistance label, because it is measured in tissue rather than on imaging.

adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.title: Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcomas: Combined Modality Therapy With Both Radiation and Surgery Improves Local Control
adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.what_it_reports: 41 consecutive localised patients, median follow-up 94 months. 10-year local control 90% overall; surgery alone was the only significant factor associated with poorer local control on univariate analysis.
adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.weight: Retrospective, single institution, and the irradiated group is the larger one (33 of 41), so indication bias runs in both directions.

adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.title: Benefit of Radiotherapy in Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma: A Propensity Score Weighted Population-based Analysis of the SEER Database
adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.what_it_reports: 172 localised patients from SEER, 2004-2012; 32% received external beam radiotherapy; propensity-weighted analysis of cancer-specific survival.
adjacent_evidence_rt_works_on_emc_somewh.weight: Population-level and propensity-weighted, which is the strongest design in this list, but it is localised disease and says nothing about metastases.

the_live_contradiction.statement: The field does not agree with itself about whether radiotherapy does anything in EMC, and both sides are recent and methodologically serious.
against: PMID 40885991 (2025, n = 171): no association between (neo)adjuvant radiotherapy and local recurrence, HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.11-2.25), p = 0.365. Read from full text.

PMID 40885991 also reports that 41.7% of irradiated patients had R1/R2 margins against 18.2% of unirradiated ones, which is the indication bias that makes the null hard to interpret in either direction.
for: PMID 31436747 (2019, n = 41): 10-year local control favours combined modality; surgery alone was the only factor significantly associated with worse local control.
PMID 27819877 (2018, n = 172, SEER, propensity-weighted): reports a cancer-specific survival benefit for external beam radiotherapy in localised disease.
PMID 33308312: a pathological complete response at 50 Gy.
PMID 36720511: a complete response sustained beyond seven years with protons.
the_live_contradiction.what_nobody_has_done: Every entry on both sides concerns the PRIMARY tumour. The contradiction has never been examined at the metastasis, at ablative dose, in the one anatomical compartment where 63% of this disease's metastatic burden actually sits.
the_live_contradiction.why_that_matters: Conventionally fractionated 50-66 Gy to a resection bed and 3-5 fraction ablative SABR to a lung nodule are different treatments with different radiobiology. A null result for the first is not evidence about the second, and the literature has been reading it as though it were.

the_natural_history_that_makes_the_case.source: PMID 19347951-adjacent record retrieved as literature/emc-rt-lung-mets/emc-two-referral-centers-drilon-2008.txt (Cancer, 2008, 2 referral centres, n = 86); read from full text
the_natural_history_that_makes_the_case.caution: The PMID for this 2008 series was NOT confirmed by the probe and must not be written into any manuscript until it is. The retrieved full text is the provenance for the figures below.
figures: First site of metastasis was the LUNG in 80% of cases.
63% had metastasis CONFINED TO THE LUNGS; a further 17% had lung disease concurrent with other sites.
34% of patients were diagnosed with, or progressed to, metastatic disease.
79% of primaries were in an extremity (62% lower, 17% upper).
Median survival after detection of metastases: 17.8 months in the 28 patients with follow-up data.
the_natural_history_that_makes_the_case.corroboration: PMID 40885991 (2025, independent cohort): of 29 patients metastatic at presentation, 27 had lung metastases and 2 had peritoneal dissemination. Read from full text.
the_natural_history_that_makes_the_case.significance_for_this_repository: RT-LUNG-DIRECTED's view states that the lung-confined fraction -- 'the actual eligibility criterion' -- is not curated and that metastatic site 'appears once in free text rather than as data'. That is true of the registry and NOT true of the primary literature: 63% lung-confined is stated outright in the retrieved full text of one series, and corroborated at 93% of the metastatic-at-presentation subgroup in another. The route's missing numerator was one fetch away.
the_natural_history_that_makes_the_case.the_tension_that_has_to_be_stated: A median survival of 17.8 months after metastasis sits badly beside the description of this disease as indolent, and the concept below must not quietly use the indolent framing and the long-survival figures while ignoring this one. It is from a 2008 cohort with 3.6 years median follow-up and it is the figure most likely to be revised by the reconstructed-IPD instrument this repository already has.
the_natural_history_that_makes_the_case.⭐_caution_lifted_2026_08_27: ⚠ *Superseded, retained:* the `caution` field above says this 2008 series' PMID 'was NOT confirmed by the probe and must not be written into any manuscript until it is'. It is confirmed now, from PubMed rather than from recollection: PMID 18951519, PMCID PMC2779719, DOI 10.1002/cncr.23978, Cancer 2008 — Memorial Sloan-Kettering and the Royal Marsden, patients treated 1975-2006, data censored 2008-03-01. The PMC full-text record was read on 2026-08-27 and the figures below stand. ⛔ The `caution` field is left in place rather than deleted, because it is the record of what was true when the probe ran.
the_natural_history_that_makes_the_case.⛔_the_word_corroborated_is_withdrawn_202: ⚠ *Superseded, retained:* '63% lung-confined is stated outright in the retrieved full text of one series, and CORROBORATED at 93% of the metastatic-at-presentation subgroup in another.' ⛔ Those two numbers are not the same quantity and the second does not corroborate the first. PMID 40885991's own words are '27 patients HAD LUNG METASTASES, and two had peritoneal dissemination' — lung INVOLVEMENT. PMID 18951519's own words separate the two: 'the first site of metastasis was the lung in 80% of cases (63% with metastasis confined to the lungs and 17% with metastasis at other sites concurrent with lung disease)'. ⇒ 93% is an involvement figure and belongs beside the 80%, not beside the 63%; the confined fraction is the LOWER of the two and is the one RT-LUNG-DIRECTED's eligibility criterion actually needs. The 27/29 reading is an UPPER BOUND. Owner of the corrected reading: research/modalities/emc-site-curation.json → `lung_confined_readings`.

the_borrowed_evidence_base.statement: Metastasis-directed radiotherapy to sarcoma lung metastases is an established, prospectively studied practice. It is simply histology-agnostic.
the_borrowed_evidence_base.read_from: Europe PMC counts in the citation index plus web-search summaries; the full texts of these sarcoma-wide papers were requested and mostly returned stub pages, so the numeric outcomes below are NOT verified here.
unverified_figures_do_not_quote: 2-year local control after SABR for sarcoma lung metastases is reported in the 83-96% range across retrospective series.
A low alpha/beta ratio of roughly 4-5 is attributed to sarcoma, which is the radiobiological argument for hypofractionation.
SABR-COMET randomised 99 patients across breast, lung, colorectal and prostate primaries and reported a median overall survival benefit; sarcoma was not a listed primary.
verified_structural_facts: Europe PMC returns 164 records for sarcoma AND lung metastases AND SABR/SBRT, and 37 with all three concepts in the TITLE -- so the sarcoma-level literature is substantial, not anecdotal.

Europe PMC returns 5 records for EMC AND stereotactic in title or abstract, of which exactly ONE concerns stereotactic treatment of EMC metastases; the other four are intracranial or cardiac primaries and a review.

A randomised phase II of SBRT in oligometastatic soft tissue sarcoma exists (Stereosarc, NCT03548428) and a prospective phase 2 of SBRT for sarcoma lung metastases exists (PMID 35987453). Neither is EMC-specific. Both identifiers came from web search and are NOT in the probe index.

correction_2026_08_10.what_was_wrong: The first version of this artifact, and the RT-MDT-LUNG grade written from it, claimed the field had made a category error: reading primary-site conventional-fractionation nulls as evidence about ablative dose to metastases. That claim was the route's stated reason for existing.
correction_2026_08_10.how_it_was_caught: By reading the full text of the 2025 comprehensive review, which was already sitting retrieved in the literature-cache branch at 112 KB when the claim was written. It was cited in this artifact as a search hit and never opened. ⛔ THE REFUTING EVIDENCE WAS IN HAND BEFORE THE CLAIM WAS MADE, and the claim was published to the route board anyway.
the_prior_art_verbatim: 'Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) may also be an option instead of surgery.'
'Local treatments such as metastasectomy or ablation can be used for oligometastatic disease, sometimes resulting in long remissions.'
'Metastasis-directed local therapy should follow uniform MDT criteria.' (in the review's own recommendations)
'The use of hypofractionated RT, delivering 3-5 Gy per fraction instead of the conventional 1.8-2 Gy per fraction, may have contributed to overcoming the intrinsic radioresistance of EMC.'

'The biologically effective dose (BED) of HDR-ISBT, calculated at 142 Gy (alpha/beta = 4), was significantly higher than conventional EBRT regimens, which typically deliver BED levels insufficient for long-term control.'
correction_2026_08_10.source: PMID 41055792, doi 10.1007/s00432-025-06316-5, J Cancer Res Clin Oncol 2025; read from retrieved full text.
correction_2026_08_10.what_survives: The observation is real and the framing was not novel. A paper arguing the rationale would be restating a 2025 review at greater length, which is not a contribution. What nobody has done is QUANTITATIVE: no one has tabulated every reported irradiated EMC metastasis with its dose, fractionation, BED and duration of local control, and no one has tested whether the alpha/beta = 4 the review borrows from generic sarcoma is consistent with the EMC observations themselves.
correction_2026_08_10.what_this_costs_the_route: RT-MDT-LUNG drops from 'a reappraisal nobody has made' to 'a synthesis nobody has assembled'. That is a much smaller claim and it may not clear the bar for a paper on its own -- see the concept memo.

additional_deliveries_found_in_the_revie.case: Lung metastases treated with SBRT 40 Gy in 10 fractions, partial radiographic response, within a 10-year course of repeated radiotherapy to spine, pelvis, limb, chest wall and clavicle.
additional_deliveries_found_in_the_revie.attribution_problem: ⚠ Superseded, retained (RESOLVED 2026-08-28 by AUT-RT-002 -- see `attribution_resolved_2026_08_28` immediately below): THE REVIEW TELLS THIS CASE TWICE, IN NEAR-IDENTICAL PARAGRAPHS, ATTRIBUTED TO TWO DIFFERENT PAPERS -- 'Qiu et al. (2014)' and 'Takagawa et al. (2022)'. At least one attribution is wrong, and Takagawa is separately cited in the same paragraph for the brachytherapy case (PMID 35494187). Do not cite this case from the review; find the primary report.
additional_deliveries_found_in_the_revie.attribution_resolved_2026_08_28: RESOLVED, by reading the review's own full text (already retrieved, literature-cache branch, literature/emc-rt-lung-mets/emc-comprehensive-review-2025.txt) rather than by search: the review's SECOND paragraph reproduces the FIRST paragraph's entire case narrative VERBATIM (same 12x7x6 cm right adductor magnus tumour, same dose-by-dose 10-year course) but relabels its opening clause 'Takagawa et al. (2022)' instead of 'Qiu et al. (2014)' -- a copy-paste/mislabelling error inside the review itself, not two competing real sources. The review's own bibliography settles it: it lists exactly ONE 2014 Qiu citation ('Qiu H, Hare M, Chen Y (2014) A case report of long-term survival of metastatic extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma treated with surgery and hypofractionated radiotherapy. J Radiother Pract 13:493-497. 10.1017/s1460396914000284') and exactly ONE 2022 Takagawa citation, which is the HDR-ISBT brachytherapy paper already in this artifact's direct_evidence array (PMID 35494187, DOI 10.5114/jcb.2022.115161) -- confirming Takagawa never published a second, lung-SBRT case. A live WebSearch on 2026-08-28 independently found a real Cambridge Core landing page at that exact title/author/journal (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-radiotherapy-in-practice/article/case-report-of-longterm-survival-of-metastatic-extraskeletal-myxoid-chondrosarcoma-treated-with-surgery-and-hypofractionated-radiotherapy/C9265B3AB9E5A73C4FD8FABAB22B30D3, authors Haoming Qiu, Mary Hare, Yuhchyau Chen, University of Rochester Medical Center) confirming the Qiu paper is real and not a review fabrication. CONFIDENCE: HIGH that Qiu et al. (2014), DOI 10.1017/S1460396914000284, is the correct and only real primary source for this case, now further corroborated by two DIRECT Europe PMC API queries dispatched 2026-08-28 (fetch-literature.yml run 33178734185, slug=emc-rt-pmid-41323055): `AUTH:"Takagawa" AND PUB_YEAR:2022 AND (TITLE/ABSTRACT:"myxoid chondrosarcoma")` returns hitCount=1, and that ONE hit IS PMID 35494187 -- empirical, not just bibliography-based, confirmation that Takagawa has no second 2022 EMC paper for the lung-SBRT case to belong to. The mirror query for `AUTH:"Qiu" AND PUB_YEAR:2014 AND (TITLE/ABSTRACT:"myxoid chondrosarcoma")` returns hitCount=0, confirming Qiu's paper is genuinely absent from Europe PMC's index (not merely unfound by search) -- consistent with, not contradicting, its real existence at Cambridge Core, since Europe PMC's coverage of small non-MEDLINE journals like Journal of Radiotherapy in Practice is incomplete. So PMID/PMCID are UNKNOWN -- the DOI and the matching Cambridge Core page are the citation. The Cambridge Core full text itself was NOT read directly (egress-blocked from this environment, same 403-class block as every other Cambridge/Wiley/Elsevier page this repo has tried), so the dose numbers below are still one layer removed from the primary text -- read from the review's paraphrase of it, cross-checked against the review's bibliography, not from the paper itself.
additional_deliveries_found_in_the_revie.why_it_matters: It is the only reported EMC LUNG metastasis treated with SBRT and given an explicit dose, and the patient far exceeded the 17.8-month figure.

additional_deliveries_found_in_the_revie.case: Radiotherapy combined with trabectedin producing near-complete regression of metastatic EMC, overall survival beyond 41 months from metastatic diagnosis.
additional_deliveries_found_in_the_revie.attribution: 'Filannino et al. (2018)' per the review; primary not retrieved.
additional_deliveries_found_in_the_revie.why_it_matters: A radiosensitisation observation, which is the RT-RT-INTENSIFY route's premise rather than this one's.

additional_deliveries_found_in_the_revie.case: Approximately 20 pulmonary nodules resected at thoracotomy; patient disease-free at 2 years.
additional_deliveries_found_in_the_revie.attribution: 'Mavrogenis et al. (2009)' per the review; primary not retrieved.
additional_deliveries_found_in_the_revie.why_it_matters: Surgical rather than radiotherapeutic, and it undercuts any tidy oligometastatic threshold -- 20 nodules is not oligometastatic by any published definition, and it worked.

dose_outcome_table.question: Extract dose, fractionation, BED and local-control duration for every reported irradiated EMC metastasis, and decide whether the assembled table surfaces anything the 2025 review (PMID 41055792) has not already said.
dose_outcome_table.method: Built ONLY from data already retrieved into this artifact -- no new fetch was dispatched for this pass. A field is 'UNKNOWN' where the source has genuinely not been read (abstract silent, full text unread or blocked), never inferred or estimated.

rows.bed_computed_here: 2 x 15 x (1 + 15/4) = 142.5 Gy, alpha/beta = 4 -- arithmetic performed here from the reported dose/fractionation, not read from any source.
rows.local_control_duration: UNKNOWN precisely -- source abstract says only 'long-term' local control at all three sites, no months/years given; needs full text.
rows.source_confidence: single-source, read from abstract via Europe PMC API

rows.modality: SABR (3 occasions, 4 dose plans) alternating with one surgical excision
rows.resolved_by: AUT-RT-001, 2026-08-28 -- full text fetched at $0 via PMC plain HTTP (see direct_evidence entry above for the exact route and run id)
rows.superseded_2026_08_28: ⚠ RESOLVED. This row previously read UNKNOWN across dose/fractions/duration ('full text ... not fetched this pass'). The four rows immediately below replace it with every dose the paper reports.

occasions.sites_treated: two abdominal nodules: a 10-mm hypodermic right-lumbar nodule and a 21-mm nodule posterior to the right psoas muscle, near the right sacroiliac joint
occasions.bed_computed_here: 5 x 8 x (1 + 8/4) = 120 Gy, alpha/beta = 4 -- arithmetic performed here, not read from the source.
occasions.local_control_duration: Complete response confirmed at the May 2024 restaging (~8 months post-SABR); both sites remained free of local relapse through the paper's last reported restaging in March 2025 (~18 months post-SABR) -- new lesions kept appearing elsewhere (oligoprogression) but never at these two sites.

occasions.sites_treated: 3 abdominal-wall nodules (12, 9 and 16 mm), found at an October 2024 restaging
occasions.local_control_duration: At the March 2025 restaging (~3 months post-SABR): complete response in 2 of these 3 nodules and a major/partial response in the third (16 mm shrank to 6 mm); the paper notes further reduction may yet appear on later imaging. No relapse reported at any of the three.

occasions.date: December 2024 (course B of 2, same clinical episode as course A -- lower dose to respect small-bowel dose constraints)
occasions.sites_treated: 2 intra-abdominal-cavity nodules (6 and 9 mm), found at the same October 2024 restaging
occasions.bed_computed_here: 5 x 7 x (1 + 7/4) = 96.25 Gy, alpha/beta = 4. Lower than the other three courses BECAUSE of the bowel constraint, not because of a different local-control intent -- Table 1 records this as the only course where the small-bowel Dmax (34.7 Gy) approaches its <35 Gy limit.
occasions.local_control_duration: Included in the same March 2025 restaging as course A above: complete or major response reported across the 5 December-2024-treated nodules collectively; the paper does not separately break out these 2 nodules' response from the other 3.

occasions.sites_treated: one new oligoprogressive 10-mm nodule of the left abdominal wall
occasions.local_control_duration: UNKNOWN -- this was the most recent treatment reported (paper received 2025-07-04, accepted 2025-08-20); no follow-up restaging after this course is described in the text.

rows.not_a_sabr_occasion: Between occasion 1 and occasion 2, a NEW 12-mm subcutaneous left-abdominal-wall nodule found in May 2024 was managed with SURGICAL EXCISION in June 2024 (pathologically confirmed EMC, Ki-67 40%), not SABR. This is the 'surgical excision' half of the abstract's 'surgical excision or SABR alone' -- no dose/fractionation applies to it.
rows.source_confidence: FULL TEXT, read directly (PMC plain HTTP fetch, 2026-08-28 -- see direct_evidence entry above). All four dose/fractionation figures are also independently confirmed by the paper's own Table 1 ('Dosimetric data of the SABR courses': Prescription dose (Gy) = 40 / 40 / 35 / 40 for the 1st-4th SABR courses respectively), so this is not resting on the running-text description alone.

rows.local_control_duration: UNKNOWN -- 'sustained symptomatic benefit' is itself UNVERIFIED per this artifact (search-engine snippet, no indexed abstract)
rows.source_confidence: UNVERIFIED -- full text blocked by Cloudflare at both the sandbox and a CI runner; do not use for anything beyond 'a delivery was reported'

dose_outcome_table.decision: NO -- the assembled table does not surface anything the 2025 review has not already said, and it is thinner than the concept paper's own §8(b) estimate implied. Of the four independently-sourced reported deliveries, only ONE (PMID 35494187) has a dose and fractionation specific enough to compute a BED, and that computation (142.5 Gy at alpha/beta=4) lands almost exactly on the review's own headline figure of '142 Gy (alpha/beta=4)' for HDR-ISBT -- which this artifact's provenance notes had NOT previously identified as the same case, since the review's quoted passage names no PMID. That identification is the one piece of new synthesis this pass produced: the review's central BED number IS PMID 35494187, not a separate unstated data point. The other three sourced deliveries (41323055, 36944557, 40885991) all lack dose and/or fractionation in what has been read so far -- two behind a full-text fetch this repository has not yet made ($0, open access, per the artifact's own outstanding list), one genuinely unreported in the source. A fifth candidate case (the twice-attributed SBRT delivery) is excluded outright rather than tabulated with an unverified attribution. A table this data-poor cannot support a dose-response argument and was never going to (concept paper §8(b) already said so); it also cannot yet support the weaker 'here is every dose anyone has reported' descriptive-appendix framing, because three of four sourced cases have no dose to report. That appendix is buildable, but only after the two outstanding $0 fetches land -- filed as new ledger items rather than dispatched in this pass.

dose_outcome_table.decision_update_2026_08_28: Two of the three outstanding items above closed in one pass (AUT-RT-001, AUT-RT-002), both by finding sources rather than by search: PMID 41323055's full text was one PMC domain away from what had already been tried (Karger 403s; plain PMC did not), and the Qiu/Takagawa conflict was resolved by reading the review's own already-cached full text rather than by fetching anything new. The table now has FOUR independently-sourced deliveries with a real dose and fractionation (PMID 35494187, PMID 41323055 x4 occasions, and the corrected Qiu-2014 lung case), against one two days ago. The doses span 4 Gy/fraction (Qiu 2014, conventional-leaning hypofractionation) through 7-8 Gy/fraction (PMID 41323055's four SABR courses, BED 96-120 Gy at alpha/beta=4) to 15 Gy/fraction (PMID 35494187's HDR-ISBT, BED 142.5 Gy) -- a real spread, not a repeat of one number, and PMID 41323055 alone now contributes four independently dosed, independently outcome-tracked deliveries in a single patient, which is more same-patient dose-response signal than this table held in total before this pass. ⛔ This does NOT by itself flip the 2026-08-27 'NO' above to a 'YES': the original decision's core objection -- that a dose-response ARGUMENT needs deliveries that vary in a way that lets outcome be compared against dose, not just deliveries that HAVE a dose -- is a judgement this update does not attempt to make, and PMID 36944557 (whole-lung EBRT, the single most on-point paper for the artifact's original lung-metastasis question) remains completely unread, still Cloudflare-blocked. What changed is factual completeness of what is already sourced, not a re-litigation of whether it adds up to a paper. That call belongs to whoever next reads this table with the concept memo in hand.

the_discrepancy_nobody_has_reconciled.statement: Median overall survival after metastasis in EMC is quoted as 17.8 months in the 2008 two-referral-centre series and as '5-7 years in modern series' by the 2025 review, which also reports a SEER-derived median OS of 48 months with 10-year OS of 10% for metastatic disease. These differ by roughly fourfold and the review uses the 17.8-month figure as the benchmark a treated patient exceeded while elsewhere stating the 5-7 year figure.
the_discrepancy_nobody_has_reconciled.why_it_matters_here: Every argument for metastasis-directed therapy in this disease rests on the patient living long enough for local control to matter. The size of that window is currently unsettled by a factor of four, and the direction of the error decides whether the strategy is compelling or marginal.
the_discrepancy_nobody_has_reconciled.who_could_settle_it: This repository already holds the instrument -- TECH-RECONSTRUCTED-IPD, whose known-answer control passes and into which no published figure has yet been digitized. Reconstructing patient-level survival from the published Kaplan-Meier curves is exactly what it is for, costs $0, and is a quantitative contribution rather than a restatement.
the_discrepancy_nobody_has_reconciled.caveat: This is a DIFFERENT paper from the radiotherapy one, and conflating them would produce a worse version of both.
measured_spread: 17.8 months — median survival after detection of metastases, 2008 two-referral-centre series (n = 86), from retrieved full text.
48 months — SEER-derived median OS for metastatic disease with 10-year OS of 10%, as reported by the 2025 review.
76 months — median OS for metastatic patients in a separate cohort ⚠ from a web-search summary, source not yet identified, NOT verified.
'5-7 years' — the 2025 review's own statement of modern-series median OS in metastatic disease.
⚠ The spread is roughly fourfold and the 2025 review quotes both ends of it in different sections.
the_discrepancy_nobody_has_reconciled.novelty_check: Checked 2026-08-10, BEFORE recommending it — which is the discipline this session failed at on the radiotherapy claim. No pooled reconstructed-IPD survival analysis of EMC was found. Multiple independent large cohorts with published Kaplan-Meier curves exist as input: the 117-case morphologic-spectrum series, the 2008 two-centre series, a SEER long-term-outcomes analysis, the US Sarcoma Collaborative database cohort (PMID 35962783) and the two-institution molecular cohort. ⚠ Identifiers other than PMID 35962783 came from web search and are not yet in the probe index; confirm each before citing.
